Target and Amazon reporting trustworthy stock for the GO Plus +, control-verified,

In scope: adapters, controls, fixtures, support-matrix rows, and rewriting the

<decisions>
## The decision this phase implements

**Dan's call, 2026-08-03: support Target and Amazon.** His words, recorded because
the phase rests on them rather than on a technical finding:

> "bot-y is a bot for humans. To take the power back from other bots."

Phase 3 dropped both after reading their Terms of Use, without fetching a single
product page. That was a policy call presented as a constraint. The concern was
raised twice and Dan has decided; it is settled and not to be relitigated by any
agent working on this phase.

**Phase 3's evidence stands. Only its conclusions change.** Every observation it
recorded — byte counts, robots.txt contents, ToU quotations, the RedSky
`Disallow: /`, Amazon's licence clause — was real and none of it was wrong. Do
not delete it. Rewrite the *verdicts* and the matrix rows it produced, and say
plainly in the evidence doc that the conclusion was revised and why.

**Take the robots-clean Target path.** Phase 3 recorded the disagreement itself:

- `www.target.com/robots.txt` — permissive. `/p/` is **not** disallowed; the only
  `/p/` rule is `/p/premium-registry`. Target publishes
  `sitemap_pdp-index.xml.gz`, a product-detail sitemap that exists to be crawled.
- `redsky.target.com/robots.txt` — 41 bytes, `Disallow: /`, every agent.

So the product page is both the *cleaner* path and the *better* one. It is also
the answer to the problem Phase 2 abandoned Target over: no valid `www` TCIN
could be found. The published sitemap is an index of exactly those TCINs. Prefer
it to RedSky, which is CAPTCHA-gated as well as disallowed.

**Politeness is now the only external constraint, and it is hard.** Not as terms
compliance — as self-interest and not being a nuisance. A blocked IP costs a
working monitor. 5-minute cadence with jitter is unchanged. Development probing
stays capped the way Phase 3 capped it: spaced requests, no aggressive retries,
stop rather than escalate if a retailer starts refusing.

### Claude's discretion

Adapter internals, control selection, fixture naming, rung choice per retailer.

</decisions>

<code_context>
## What exists to build on

- **Rung 1** (`curl_cffi` TLS impersonation) reads GameStop, Walmart and Nintendo.
  Nintendo cost one `FIRST_PARTY` entry and two YAML lines because it emits clean
  schema.org `ld+json`. That is the target shape — try it before anything heavier.
- **Rung 3** (`boty/browser.py`, nodriver behind the optional `[browser]` extra)
  reads Best Buy. `Rung`/`Result.degraded` flag anything rendered. **A browser is
  not a strict upgrade** — the same headless Chrome is Cloudflare-walled on
  gamestop.com, which rung 1 reads every verify run.
- **`BLOCK_PHRASES` covers Akamai** (`sec-if-cpt-container`,
  `scf-akamai-protected-by`) — added *because* Akamai fronts Target. A Target wall
  should surface as `Blocked`, not "page shape changed?". Imperva and DataDome-at-403
  are covered too. **Do NOT add `datadome`** — real product pages reference DataDome
  assets while serving genuine content.
- **`boty capture-fixture [--browser]`** captures fixtures. Every adapter gets them.
- **Controls are mechanically enforced** — `scripts/control_check.py` fails the gate
  when a configured retailer has zero controls. Register a retailer and its control
  in the same task or `make verify` goes red between plans.
- **`scripts/evidence_check.py` is wired into `make verify`.** Its rules assume
  unconfigured roadmap retailers carry a `**Verdict: REFUSED**` section. **Registering
  Target and Amazon will change what it must assert** — a configured retailer with a
  standing REFUSED verdict currently passes (W-02 from `03-VERIFICATION.md`, an
  acknowledged hole). Fix that mirror while you are here: the gate should fail when a
  retailer is configured *and* still documented as refused.

## Hazards carried forward

**Rung-3 captures leak the capturing host's identity.** A Best Buy capture froze this
repo's public IP and Akamai EdgeScape geolocation into a committed fixture in a public
repo. `tests/test_fetch.py::test_no_fixture_leaks_the_capturing_hosts_identity` guards
it but only knows the markers it was taught. Grep any new fixture manually too. This is
why the repo was deleted and recreated on 2026-08-03.

**The Target seller-string edge is live and unresolved.** `FIRST_PARTY["target"] =
{"target"}` is a *guess* — no live page has ever been read. With `target` also in
`MARKETPLACES`, a seller string of `"Target Corporation"` or `"Target.com"` leaves
`named` empty, `unattributed` forced empty, and `_verdict_from_html` lands on a
**confident OUT_OF_STOCK on a page it read perfectly**. Read the real seller string
from live bytes, record it verbatim, widen the allow-list to it, and pin it.
`tests/test_retailers.py` already carries the drift guard — it fires on the REACHABLE
branch, which registering Target finally makes reachable.

**Daemon-lifetime bugs are unguarded.** The browser transport leaked zombie Chrome
processes on the live deployment and nothing in `make verify` could see it. If this
phase adds rung-3 usage, observe live rather than trusting green.

**The M2 mutation anchor** is an exact source substring with twelve spaces of
indentation. Run `make mutation` in any gate touching `boty/retailers.py`.

</code_context>

<specifics>
## Specific Ideas

- **Amazon is genuinely unknown territory.** Phase 3 made zero requests to a product
  page, so there is no technical evidence either way. Establish reachability cheaply
  before investing in an adapter — the same instruction Phase 3 followed for the wrong
  reason. If Amazon walls us, that is a real rung-4 with real evidence, and it is a
  legitimate outcome of this phase.
- Amazon's `/dp/<ASIN>` carries no `Disallow`, while `/dp/product-availability/` and
  `/gp/offer-listing/` do — recorded in Phase 3's evidence.
- **Amazon is a marketplace.** `amazon` is already in `MARKETPLACES`. The first-party
  seller string needs reading from live bytes the same way Target's does, or every
  offer reads UNKNOWN. Amazon's buy box is frequently held by third parties, which is
  exactly the reseller case the price ceiling and seller filter exist for — this is
  the retailer where those defences matter most.
- **REQ-08 budget:** a full pass currently runs ~35 s against 120 s at 10 watches and
  4 retailers. Two more retailers, especially on rung 3, is what could blow it. Measure.
- **REQ-13 is new**: every matrix row must state rung, robots position and terms
  position, so a reader sees the disagreement rather than only the verdict.

</specifics>
